canonical_title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick (adapted by Andy Hopkins and Joc Potter)
card_summary: A bounty hunter tracks escaped androids across a depopulated Earth, testing them for empathy they may only be faking — while questioning whether he himself has any left. This archive item is an English-learner adaptation.
page_summary:
On a dying Earth emptied by radioactive fallout, most who remain keep artificial animals as status symbols and tokens of a fading empathy. Rick Deckard hunts fugitive Nexus-6 androids for bounty, distinguishing them from humans with the Voigt-Kampff empathy test. As he retires one android after another, the line between the hunter and the hunted, the human and the manufactured, grows harder to hold.

The novel makes empathy the sole criterion of the human, then keeps eroding it — the androids lack it, but so, at moments, does Deckard, while the ersatz religion of Mercerism offers a mediated, possibly fraudulent version of fellow-feeling. Reality itself is unstable: mood is dialed on the Penfield organ, animals may be electric, prophets may be actors. The book asks whether empathy can be tested, faked, or lost, and what remains of the human when it is.

This particular archive record is not the original 1968 novel but an Oxford Bookworms graded-reader adaptation for English learners; the underlying work is one of PKD's most influential and the basis for the film Blade Runner.
